builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: RSIV-Harness: A Recursive Self-Improvement Harness Framework for Open-Domain Conversational Text-to-Visualization
summary: Replaces a static, manually designed agent harness with a procedure that rewrites prompts, tools, or control logic from the agent's own failure traces while keeping model weights fixed. Costs extra offline evaluation cycles and LLM calls for failure analysis and harness validation, plus the added complexity of anchor and memory checks to keep revisions stable. Can fail if self-revisions overfit to the benchmark or trace distribution, if validation checks miss regressions, or if failure traces are unrepresentative, silently degrading production behavior.
rationale: The method is infrastructure-light and model-agnostic, so a small team can trial it, but the gains are reported on a single new benchmark and require validation on the reader's own workloads before production use.
technique: Recursive self-improvement of agent harness from failure traces

claims.statement: Replaces a static, manually designed agent harness with a procedure that rewrites prompts, tools, or control logic from the agent's own failure traces while keeping model weights fixed. Costs extra offline evaluation cycles and LLM calls for failure analysis and harness validation, plus the added complexity of anchor and memory checks to keep revisions stable. Can fail if self-revisions overfit to the benchmark or trace distribution, if validation checks miss regressions, or if failure traces are unrepresentative, silently degrading production behavior.
One self-improvement round improved all six metrics on ODAC-Vis, with +28.02 points executability and +34.01 points chart structure over the seed harness.
